author: Krishani Dhanji
description:
Four countries call situation ‘entirely reversible’ in joint statement as flooding exacerbates humanitarian crisis

Australia, Canada, the United Kingdom and Italy have urged Israel to allow critical humanitarian aid to enter Gaza, describing the situation on the ground as “dire”.

The four countries released a joint statement on Monday morning, urging Israel to allow 150,000 tents and other vital supplies being held at the border into Gaza ahead of winter.

Continue reading...
title: Australia, UK, Canada and Italy urge Israel to allow critical aid to Gaza ahead of winter

author: Michael Sainato
description:
Mohamed Yusuf is fighting for his life after alleged attack by passenger who said he did not like driver’s first name

A Somali-American Uber driver was allegedly brutally assaulted by a passenger in Hopkins, Minnesota, on Saturday, in what his family says “appears to be a hate crime”.

The driver, Mohamed Yusuf, is currently hospitalized and fighting for his life, his family told the Somali Brief, a digital news site run by two Somali American journalists. The driver’s cousin, Abdinasir Ali told the outlet that the alleged attack took place early Saturday after a passenger in Hopkins, a suburban city south-west of Minneapolis, asked Yusuf’s name and then said he did not like the name Mohamed.

Contin
title: Somali-American Uber driver brutally assaulted in alleged hate crime in Minnesota

author: Ramon Antonio Vargas
description:
Mississippi Democrat points to commitments Trump made: lower prices, halt endless wars and release Epstein files

After recently becoming the first Mississippi Democrat elected to the US Senate in more than four decades, Scott Colom pledged to try to ensure Donald Trump “follows through on the commitments” he made while successfully running for a second presidency in 2024.

Colom, while being interviewed by CNN host Dana Bash on Sunday, alluded to various campaign promises made by Trump – including lowering consumer prices, halting the seemingly endless wars waged under other presidential administrations, and fully releasing files related to the prosecution of Jeffrey Epstein, the late accused sex trafficker whose social circle encompassed the US and global elite.
title: Senator-elect Scott Colom vows to ensure Trump follows through on his promises

author: Marina Dunbar
description:
Progressive US senator calling for more inclusion within Democratic caucus cites openness to change among peers

Democratic US senator Chris Van Hollen on Sunday escalated his bid to lead his party’s incoming Senate majority rather than Chuck Schumer, asserting that he has a path to victory amid a dedicated campaign that includes a series of television appearances.

Van Hollen, a Maryland progressive, appeared on Sunday on CNN, ABC and Fox News as he continues to make his case for why his peers in the Senate should reject Schumer, who has led the Democratic caucus for nearly a decade.

Cont
title: Chris Van Hollen says he has path to win Senate leader over Chuck Schumer

author: Ben Quinn Political Correspondent
description:
Total of 75 have already signed letter to Burnham opposing plans as discontent also grows over Europe and welfare changes

As many as 100 Labour MPs could sign a letter opposing the giant Rosebank oilfield, as discontent among backbenchers looks likely to surge this week, with rebellions also brewing over Europe and welfare changes.

A total of 75 MPs have already signed the private letter, which is expected to be delivered in the next fortnight to Andy Burnham as part of a campaign in which Labour MPs from the party’s 2024 intake are playing a significant role.

Continue reading...
title: Labour rebellion over Rosebank oilfield expected to top 100 MPs

author: Michael Sainato
description:
Democratic senator Chris Van Hollen says Trump administration hasn’t properly invested existing funds

Donald Trump’s administration on Sunday blamed the travel chaos stemming from Friday’s four-hour nationwide flight stoppage on prior presidents as well as a lack of congressional funding – though a Democratic senator argued that the Trump administration hasn’t properly invested all of the funds it has already been given to implement needed air travel infrastructure upgrades.

“I take responsibility for what was given to me by prior administrations,” the US transportation secretary, Sean Duffy, told CNN’s Dana Bash, a day after he said routine but necessary maintenance botched by a contractor had caused Friday’s Federal Aviation Administration (FAA)
title: Transportation secretary Sean Duffy blames prior presidents and Congress for flight stoppage

author: Rob Davies
description:
Chain restocks stores in operation named after singer of I Will Survive after US owners release funds

Poundland’s under-fire US owners have released funds to help the stricken discount chain restock shelves temporarily, keeping hopes of a rescue deal alive in the run-up to crunch talks with the government.

In an emergency resupply effort codenamed “Operation Gloria” by senior Poundland staff, about 16m grocery items were dispatched to 600 shops in the UK and Ireland over the weekend.

Continue reading...
title: Poundland pins rescue hopes on Yorkshire Tea, Pot Noodle and Gloria Gaynor

author: Harry Taylor
description:
UKHSA warns of health impact on those vulnerable to cold and urges people to check in with neighbours

Cold weather warnings have been issued for parts of the UK, as alerts for the risk to health services are due to begin on Sunday evening.

The Met Office issued yellow weather warnings for ice for central and eastern Scotland from 6pm on Sunday evening until 10am on Monday.

Continue reading...
title: Cold and health alerts issued for Scotland and northern England as snow and ice expected

author: Dan Sabbagh Defence and security editor
description:
HMS Vengeance’s 217-day tour raises questions about slow pace of maintenance of ageing fleet and impact on crew

A Trident nuclear submarine has concluded a record seven-month deployment, returning to the Faslane naval base in Scotland, where its crew are expected to be greeted by senior members of the government .

HMS Vengeance began its patrol on 12 April and spent 217 days submerged before returning on Sunday, leaving the country when Keir Starmer was in Downing Street and Manchester United were third in the Premier League.

Continue reading...
title: Trident nuclear submarine concludes record underwater deployment

author: George Chidi in Atlanta
description:
Activists have been shouting about economic issues for years – in January they will expect lawmakers to respond

Stonecrest is resolutely middle class. About six out of 10 of its voters cast ballots in the 2026 election and about 90% of them voted for Democrats, according to election figures. And they have often been overlooked by Georgia’s Republican establishment.

The fundraiser Keisha Lance Bottoms held at the Privi event center and retreat in suburban Atlanta in September didn’t draw a lot of attention. But Stonecrest, by one measure the largest city in the United States with a non-Hispanic Black population above 90%, tends to roll under the radar.

Continue reading...
title: Black voters helped Democrats win in Georgia. Now they expect to be heard

author: Melody Schreiber
description:
Experts warn that sweeping changes elevate health secretary RFK Jr’s anti-vaccine agenda and personal profit

The Trump administration is finalizing a rule to reimburse doctors who diagnose, treat and counsel patients with side effects from vaccines in what experts believe is an attempt to undermine trust in vaccines and to create an evidence base on their purported risks.

Robert F Kennedy Jr, the secretary of the US Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), also announced the creation of a vaccine “injury” research center at the National Institutes of Health and has sought to reshape the Vaccine Injury Compensation Program (VICP) – actions that point to Kennedy’s longtime activism against vaccination as well as the profits he and his network have made from vaccine lawsuits.
title: Trump administration planning to reimburse doctors treating vaccine ‘injury’

author: Ben Quinn Political correspondent
description:
MP says party is being squeezed by arrival of ‘more plausible’ Labour leader in Andy Burnham

Reform UK has been losing support to Labour after “a very difficult year,” Danny Kruger has admitted, just over 12 months after his defection to Nigel Farage’s party.

The MP, who has been tasked with preparing Reform for government, denied that he regretted jumping from the Conservatives as recent polls indicated a revival under Kemi Badenoch.

Continue reading...
title: Reform UK losing support to Labour after ‘difficult year’, says Danny Kruger

author: Tom McIlroy in Manila
description:
‘We think dialogue is a good thing,’ Australian PM says after German chancellor urges the US to work with Europe for peace in Ukraine

Australia has endorsed this week’s historic summit between Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin in China, even as European leaders warn that the US president must not make major concessions over the war in Ukraine.

The three-way summit is planned to take place in Shenzhen, where the leaders will gather for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) meeting. Likened to the 1945 summit at Yalta, the Ukrainian president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, has warned the talks must not lead to a redistribution of influence among world powers or the abandonment of his country, more than four years into the war sparked by Putin’s full-scale invasion.
title: Anthony Albanese welcomes Trump-Xi-Putin summit – even as European leaders express reservations

author: Tom McIlroy in Manila
description:
Prime minister says he and Chris Bowen were having ‘light-hearted banter’ when they were caught discussing where they keep their phones

  • Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast

Anthony Albanese has apologised for a hot-mic gaffe at the UN climate talks in Turkey, saying he regretted being overheard discussing mobile phone radiation and “dicks” in a candid conversation.

“I of course regret that. I apologise,” Albanese said during a visit to the Australian warship HMAS Stalwart in the Philippines on Sunday.

title: Anthony Albanese apologises for hot-mic gaffe after Coalition criticises ‘locker-room talk’

author: Andrew Messenger
description:
Party’s NSW leader Mike Newman says contenders are ‘people from the real world’ and not ‘career politicians’

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The failed federal Liberal candidate Katherine Deves, who campaigned to exclude transgender women from women’s sport, will stand for One Nation at next year’s New South Wales election.

Deves was among four NSW Legislative Council candidates announced by One Nation’s NSW leader, Mike Newman, on Sunday.

Continue reading...
title: Katherine Deves among four NSW upper house candidates revealed by One Nation

author: Stephanie Convery
description:
Volatile weather predicted after storms on Saturday, with a man in his 20s struck by lightning while swimming on NSW Central Coast

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Dangerous and severe “supercell” thunderstorms with the potential for giant hail and destructive winds were forecast for parts of New South Wales on Sunday, as volatile weather continued in the eastern states over the weekend.

Storms dumped heavy rain across large parts of northern and eastern NSW and much of Queensland on Saturday, with strong winds recorded up to 98km/h in Goulburn and rainfall totals of between 30mm and 50mm in the Coffs Harbour area.
title: Thunderstorms, giant hail and powerful winds forecast for NSW as wild weather hits east coast
